subject.title: [Bug]: `openclaw models auth login` on node host writes OAuth token locally instead of syncing to gateway

question: Should `openclaw models auth login` on a node host connected to a non-loopback gateway fail closed before provider auth starts, or should OpenClaw add a gateway-owned credential forwarding/sync path?
rationale: Both valid fixes affect where OAuth credentials are minted and stored; automation should not choose a cross-host credential-transfer policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Fail Closed On Remote Node Hosts
options.body: Block the login before OAuth/token creation when `node.json` points at a non-loopback gateway and tell the operator to run auth on the gateway host.

options.title: Design Gateway Credential Sync
options.body: Keep the workflow convenient by adding an explicit gateway API for credential transfer, with security review and upgrade tests.

options.title: Accept Node-Local Auth Writes
options.body: Document that node-host auth login affects only the node-local store and require operators to authenticate directly on the gateway.

recommendation.title: Fail Closed On Remote Node Hosts
recommendation.body: Block the login before OAuth/token creation when `node.json` points at a non-loopback gateway and tell the operator to run auth on the gateway host.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest current routing signal from recent auth/node-host history and the prior maintainer remote-node OAuth guard attempt.
